tested_scope: One deterministic local Node.js v22.16.0 negative-control probe of the existing minimal escape-aware pre-materialization source-order scanner mechanism class using per-object-frame decoded-key exact seen/NFC state over exactly one fixed same-object JSON source containing two distinct decoded keys that NFC-normalize to the same string: {"é":1,"e\u0301":2}.
mechanism: The scanner maintains a structural stack; each object frame owns an exact decoded-key seen set and an NFC map. A source-order JSON string token is treated as a key when the next non-whitespace source character is a colon and the top frame is an object. Exact duplicate decoded keys are rejected; otherwise a second distinct decoded key whose NFC normalization matches a prior key in the same object frame is rejected before whole-document materialization.
inference: For this exact fixed source, the object-frame NFC map detects that decoded keys é and é are distinct strings but normalize to the same NFC string and rejects the second key before JSON.parse materialization. Combined only with prior own-role exact-duplicate and sibling exact-reuse controls, this narrows the local mechanism toward object-scoped collision handling; it does not establish that NFC state is correctly scoped across sibling objects or any broader JSON correctness property.
scope_guard: Evidence is limited to exactly one fixed same-object NFC-equivalent distinct-key source, this minimal object-frame scoped scanner mechanism class, and Node.js v22.16.0. It does not establish cross-object NFC-map scoping, arbitrary nesting, broader array semantics, malformed JSON behavior, Unicode edge completeness, parser differentials, performance, or standards-complete duplicate-key detection.
